text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High tail latency + 503 spike observed on Dedicated pool `dp-west-3` starting at 3624509876. Error rate 12% over 5m, requests/sec doubled vs baseline. Auto-scaler reports sustained queue growth. Paging on-call.

oncall-alex: Acknowledged. I'm looking at the pool dashboard. QPS is dominated by a single tenant (tenant: shopwise-prod) — they account for ~65% of tokens.

sre-rita: On it. Suggest we enable QoS per-tenant caps and temporarily raise pool max_nodes to handle surge while throttling noisy customer. Propose: cap per-tenant QPS to 120, bump pool max_nodes from 16 -> 24 for 10m window. Thoughts?

eng-runtime-jamie: +1 to QoS + temporary capacity. Also recommend increasing autoscale cooldown to 90s to avoid thrashing. Default was 30s.

oncall-alex: If we do cap, we should also adjust quota bucketing so other tenants don't starve. Implement token-bucket with burst=200, rate=120 for tenant.

pm-lina: Heads-up: shopwise-prod is a paying customer on a committed plan. If we throttle them we should notify support & PMs to prepare comms.

support-omar: I'm drafting a message for the account team. Can we confirm expected impact if we cap to 120 qps? Roughly 30% request shedding for their peak windows.

sre-rita: Running commands now.

sre-rita: ```
# increase pool max nodes
redwoodctl dedicated pool update dp-west-3 --max-nodes 24 --note "emergency surge bump"
# set per-tenant qos
redwoodctl qos set --pool dp-west-3 --tenant shopwise-prod --rate 120 --burst 200
# set autoscaler cooldown
redwoodctl autoscale update dp-west-3 --cooldown 90
```

sre-rita: Commands applied — API returned 202 for all. Scaling actions in progress (pods launching).

oncall-alex: Observing reduced queue depth, latency starting to decrease. Error rate down to 4% after ~90s. Looks promising.

eng-runtime-jamie: Added a temporary routing policy: shift ~20% of new requests from dp-west-3 to dp-us-1 to spread load. Implemented using `route-policy surge-shim`.

incident-bot: Deploy event recorded: route-policy surge-shim activated by eng-runtime-jamie at 3624509950.

pm-lina: Support: please send the drafted note to account ops with the explanation that this is a protective QoS cap to keep the service available. Offer to coordinate a dedicated capacity upgrade if they need sustained throughput.

support-omar: Sent to account ops and cc'd oncall. Message includes impact estimate and rollback plan.

oncall-alex: Agreed checklist for runbook: 1) Monitor 5m error rate <5% 2) No new customer-facing incidents for 15m 3) If shopwise requests, escalate to sales for capacity plan. If errors reoccur, revert QoS and open full incident.

eng-runtime-jamie: Setting alert to notify if scaled nodes > 22 for > 15m so we don't run sustained overprovisioning.

sre-rita: Also added a temporary quota bump for internal health checks so they don't spur more autoscale: `--tenant infra-health +10qps`

oncall-alex: Timeline summary: 3624509876 alert -> 3624509890 oncall ack -> 3624509905 QoS + bump cmds -> 3624509950 route policy -> 3624509999 stable with error rate down.

pm-lina: Good work. Can someone own the postmortem and include the decision rationale (why QoS first vs immediate scaling), the command runbook, and customer comms?

sre-rita: I can draft the postmortem and include the CLI snippets and metrics. Will tag eng-runtime and product.

oncall-alex: I'll hand off monitoring to the next on-call in 45m. Please update this thread with any changes.

incident-bot: NOTE: Temporary QoS rules and max-nodes bump scheduled to auto-revert at 3624510476 (1 hour). Manual extension requires `redwoodctl` approval 2FA.

eng-runtime-jamie: Final: set rollback criteria — revert bump if sustained usage falls below 60% of previous peak for 20m and error rate <2%.

support-omar: Logged communication with account ops. No immediate customer escalations.

oncall-alex: Closing active mitigation — monitoring mode. Will escalate if regressions. :white_check_mark:
